divergence: jsonata-js takes substring(0, length-1) for F&O 4.7.5 bullet 12 and so leaves one character of a multi-character decimal-separator behind ("07a"); the spec removes the decimal-separator itself (XPath 3.1 F&O 4.7.5, jsntrs-0kg)
unresolved: The "decimal-separator" option is set to a multi-character string. XPath 3.1 F&O 4.7.1 types it as "A single character", so this is not a well-formed decimal format and F&O defines no behaviour for it. jsonata.org does license some values F&O 4.7.1 would reject — its own worked examples are $formatNumber(0.14, "###pm", {"per-mille": "pm"}) => "140pm" and $formatNumber(1234.5678, "①①.①①①e①", {"zero-digit": "⑟"}) => "①②.③④⑦e②" — but it states no rule, and this case is not either of those shapes. Regression pin over jsntrs' current behaviour, not a derived answer — see README.md and jsntrs-qr9.
